title: Electrical energy and power
summary: Learn about electrical energy, power, the kWh, brightness, and electrical safety.
cards.0.p: A device converts electrical energy into another form of energy. A lamp converts it into light, a motor into motion, and a heater into heat. Energy is conserved, but some of it usually goes to heat.
cards.0.key: Energy is not destroyed. It only changes form. A charging battery converts electricity into chemical energy.
cards.0.once.soru: What does a plugged-in fan mostly convert electrical energy into?
cards.0.once.secenekler.0.neden: The motor turns the blades. Some of the energy also goes to heat.
cards.0.once.secenekler.1.neden: The device that converts it into light is a lamp.
cards.0.once.secenekler.2.neden: What converts it into chemical energy is a charging battery.
cards.1.p: Voltage is the energy transferred to 1 C of charge: 1 V = 1 J/C. In a time t, a charge of q = I·t passes. So the energy used is W = V·I·t.
cards.1.key: Suppose a laptop charger runs at 20 V and 3 A for 30 minutes. The energy used is W = 20 · 3 · 1800 = 108 000 J.
cards.2.h: Power: P = V·I and its two siblings
cards.2.p: The energy used per unit time is called power. Power is found with P = W/t = V·I, and its unit is the watt. Substituting V = I·R gives the relations P = I²·R and P = V²/R.
cards.2.once.soru: On the same 220 V outlet, does a 100 W bulb or a 60 W bulb draw more current?
cards.2.once.secenekler.0.neden: I = P/V. At the same voltage, more power means more current.
cards.2.once.secenekler.1.neden: The voltage is the same. Less power means less current.
cards.2.once.secenekler.2.neden: Since their powers are different, their currents are different too.
cards.3.h: I²R in series, V²/R in parallel
cards.3.p: In a series connection the current is shared, and P = I²·R is used. So the larger resistor uses more power. In a parallel connection the voltage is shared, and P = V²/R is used. So the smaller resistor uses more power.
cards.3.key: Of a 40 W and a 100 W bulb connected in series, the 40 W one glows brighter.
cards.4.p: In a resistor carrying current, electrons collide with atoms and electrical energy turns into heat. This is called Joule heating and is found with Q = I²·R·t. In a heater this heat is wanted, but in cables it is a loss.
cards.4.key: Heat grows with the square of the current. That is why electricity is transmitted at high voltage and low current.
cards.5.p: A source delivers a power of P = ε·I to the circuit. Of this, I²·r turns into heat in the internal resistance, and I²·R reaches the external resistor: ε·I = I²·R + I²·r.
cards.5.key: Going further: the power delivered to the external resistor is greatest when R = r. In a short circuit (R ≈ 0) it is zero.
cards.5.once.soru: Why does a battery that runs for a long time heat up?
cards.5.once.secenekler.0.neden: The current also passes through the battery's internal resistance. The power used there is P = I²·r. So in a time t, an energy of I²·r·t turns into heat inside the battery.
cards.5.once.secenekler.1.neden: The heat forms inside the battery itself.
cards.5.once.secenekler.2.neden: A battery's voltage does not increase as it is used.
cards.6.p: On the bill, energy is measured in kilowatt-hours. A device that runs for 1 hour at a power of 1 kW uses 1 kWh of energy. The amount to pay is the kWh multiplied by the unit price.
cards.6.key: 1 kWh is 3.6 million J. If a 2 kW heater runs 3 hours a day for 30 days, it uses 180 kWh. If the unit price is 3 TL, the cost is 540 TL.
cards.6.etk.soru: Change the device's power, the daily use, and the unit price. What is your 30-day bill?
cards.7.p: 220 V, 1100 W on a label says that 1100 W is used at 220 V. This gives I = P/V = 5 A and R = V²/P = 44 Ω.
cards.7.svg#7: If you plug it into 110 V (R constant):
cards.7.key: The power on the label is valid only at the voltage on the label.
cards.8.p: The brightness of a bulb is set by the power it uses. When two identical bulbs are connected in series, each gets V/2 and glows dimly at a power of P/4. When they are connected in parallel, each glows at a power of P.
cards.8.key: If one bulb in series is short-circuited, the remaining bulbs glow brighter.
cards.8.once.soru: You connect two identical bulbs in parallel. How does each glow compared with a single bulb?
cards.8.once.secenekler.0.neden: Each bulb still gets the battery's full voltage, and its power stays P. The battery, however, delivers twice the current.
cards.8.once.secenekler.1.neden: Dimming happens in a series connection.
cards.8.once.secenekler.2.neden: Since the voltage does not increase, the power does not increase either.
cards.9.p: The outlets and lamps in a home are connected in parallel. Each device gets 220 V and can be switched on and off separately. Every device that is switched on increases the total current.
cards.9.key: As you switch on more devices, the equivalent resistance decreases and the total current increases. That is why plugging many devices into one outlet is dangerous.
cards.9.once.soru: You turn off the lamp in the living room. The fridge keeps running. Why?
cards.9.once.secenekler.0.neden: Each device has its own branch. When one is switched on or off, the other is not affected.
cards.9.once.secenekler.1.neden: In series, turning off the lamp would break the circuit, and the fridge would stop too.
cards.9.once.secenekler.2.neden: All the devices in a home get the same 220 V.
cards.10.p: A fuse is connected in series with the live wire and cuts the circuit when the current limit (e.g. 16 A) is exceeded. An overload or a short circuit can heat the cables and start a fire.
cards.10.svg#3: overload or short circuit → current exceeds the limit
cards.10.key: In a short circuit, a path with almost zero resistance forms and the current becomes very large. Do not replace a blown fuse with a fuse of a higher rating.
cards.11.p: A residual-current device (RCD) compares the outgoing and the returning current. If the difference is about 30 mA, it cuts the circuit. Grounding, in turn, drains leakage current on a metal casing into the ground.
cards.11.key: Do not touch an outlet with wet hands. Do not use damaged cables, and do not overload a power strip.
cards.11.once.soru: Current leaked onto the metal casing of a washing machine. If the casing is grounded, where does the current go?
cards.11.once.secenekler.0.neden: Grounding is a path with very small resistance. The leakage current flows through it instead of through you.
cards.11.once.secenekler.1.neden: On a grounded casing, the current chooses the ground wire, which has very small resistance.
cards.11.once.secenekler.2.neden: Leaked current always finds a path. Grounding makes that path safe.
cards.12.p: The ratio of useful energy to energy used is called efficiency. An incandescent bulb converts about 5% of the energy into light. An LED gives the same light with much less power.
cards.12.key: Efficiency can never exceed 100%. A roughly 9 W LED is enough in place of a 60 W incandescent bulb.
cards.13.p:
• W = V·I·t and P = V·I = I²R = V²/R.
• I²R is used in series, V²/R in parallel.
• Power sets the brightness.
• 1 kWh is 3.6×106 J.
• Home wiring is parallel.
• A fuse protects the cable. An RCD and grounding protect people.
quiz.0.q: In how many seconds does a 2000 W kettle heat 1.5 kg of water from 20 °C to 100 °C? (Specific heat of water 4200 J/kg·°C, no heat loss)
quiz.0.e: The heat needed is Q = m·c·ΔT = 1.5·4200·80 = 504 000 J. The electrical energy equals P·t. So t = 504 000 / 2000 = 252 s (about 4.2 minutes).
quiz.1.q: Does each expression or unit give energy or power? Put it in the right group.
quiz.1.e: Power is energy per unit time. Its unit is the watt, that is J/s, and it is found with P = V·I = I²·R. Multiplying power by time gives energy: W = V·I·t and Q = I²·R·t. The kWh is also a unit of energy, because it is power multiplied by time.
quiz.2.q: Match each home electrical safety measure with its job.
quiz.2.ciftler.0.1: Cuts the circuit on excess current
quiz.2.ciftler.2.1: Carries leakage current from casing to ground
quiz.2.ciftler.3.1: Each device gets the same 220 V
quiz.2.e: A fuse opens the circuit when the current limit is exceeded. A residual-current device compares the current going out on the live wire with the current returning on the neutral. Grounding takes leakage current to the ground instead of through you. In parallel wiring, each device gets the same voltage.
quiz.3.q: Identical bulbs K and L are connected in parallel with each other. This pair is connected in series with an identical bulb M and attached to an ideal battery. What is the order of brightness?
quiz.3.e: The total current I passes through M, and I/2 passes through each of K and L. Since P = I²R, the power of M is 4 times that of K or L.
quiz.3.y.0: K and L on the parallel branches share the current. So less current passes through each of them than through M on the main branch.
quiz.3.y.1: M on the main branch carries the total current, and each parallel branch gets half of it. So M glows brighter.
quiz.3.y.2: Since K and L are identical and in parallel, they draw equal currents and glow equally.
A:ozet: Charge the phone and compare the brightness of the bulbs. Heat the wire, read the label, and lower the bill. Switch to LED without blowing the fuse.
A:adimlar.0.metin: The energy transferred is found with W = V · I · t. The charger delivers 5 V and 2 A. Transfer 36 000 J of energy to the phone.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.tamam: W = 5 · 2 · 3600 = 36 000 J. 1 hour is 3600 seconds. Do not forget to convert minutes to seconds.
A:adimlar.1.metin: The brightness of a bulb is set by its power. The resistances of the bulbs are 2 Ω and 4 Ω. In series the current is shared, so P = I² · R is used. In parallel the voltage is shared, so P = V² / R is used. Try both connections.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.soru: Which bulb is brighter when they are in series?
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: In series the current is shared, and since P = I² · R, the smaller resistor uses less power. The 2 Ω bulb glows brighter only in parallel.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: In series the same current passes through both, and since P = I² · R, the larger resistor uses more power. In parallel, P = V² / R, so the 2 Ω bulb glows brighter.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The resistances are different. So they use different powers at the same current.
A:adimlar.2.metin: Heat is found with Q = I² · R · t. A 10 Ω wire gives 600 J of heat in 1 minute at a current of 1 A. Make the heat 4 times as large.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.tamam: When the current doubles, the heat becomes 2² = 4 times as large: 2² · 10 · 60 = 2400 J. That is why fuses and cable thickness matter.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.ipucu: Heat increases with the square of the current.
A:adimlar.3.metin: The heater's label says 220 V, 2000 W. Its resistance is R = V² / P = 24.2 Ω and does not change. We plug the heater into a 110 V outlet.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.soru: How many watts does the heater use at 110 V?
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: The voltage was halved, but power is proportional to V². The square of one half is one quarter.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: The power on the label is valid only at 220 V.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The resistance is constant, so P = V² / R = 110² / 24.2 = 500 W. When the voltage is halved, the power drops to one quarter.
A:adimlar.4.metin: Energy (kWh) is power (kW) multiplied by time (hours). A 1.5 kW air conditioner runs for 30 days, and 1 kWh costs 3 TL. Adjust the daily use so that the monthly cost does not exceed 270 TL.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.tamam: If it runs 2 hours a day, it uses 1.5 · 2 · 30 = 90 kWh, and the cost is 90 · 3 = 270 TL. Halving the time also halves the bill.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.ipucu: 270 TL / 3 TL makes 90 kWh. How many hours is 90 / (1.5 · 30)?
A:adimlar.5.metin: The fuse is rated 16 A, and the 2000 W heater is on. Switch on one more device next to it, but do not blow the fuse.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.tamam: 9.1 A + 5 A makes about 14.1 A, and this value is below the limit. With the kettle the total would be 19.1 A, and the fuse would blow. A fuse protects the cable from overheating.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.ipucu: The current of each device is found with I = P / 220. The total current must not exceed 16 A.
A:adimlar.6.metin: A 60 W incandescent bulb and a 9 W LED give the same light. Switch to LED.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.soru: If it is on 5 hours a day, how much energy does the LED save in a year?
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: That only looks at the 9 W the LED uses. The difference is 60 − 9 = 51 W.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: 51 is the difference in watts. It has to be multiplied by the number of hours and days.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The difference is 51 W. 51 W · 5 hours · 365 days makes about 93 000 Wh, that is 93 kWh.
A:kapanis.0: Electrical energy is found with W = V · I · t. Power is P = V · I = I² · R = V² / R.
A:kapanis.1: Power sets the brightness. In series the larger resistor glows brighter, and in parallel the smaller one does.
A:kapanis.2: Heat is found with Q = I² · R · t. When the current doubles, the heat becomes four times as large.
A:kapanis.3: The kWh is a unit of energy. The bill is power multiplied by time and by the unit price.
A:kapanis.4: Home wiring is parallel, and the fuse limits the total current. An LED gives the same light with much less energy.
